analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail: The Torah source text mentions several concepts but does NOT call any of them a 'bechina' of another. The concepts present are: (1) גְּזֵרָה — the divine decree; (2) מַזָּל — the person's celestial representative who sees the decree even when the person does not (Megillah 3); (3) הַסְתָּרָה — the soul's impulse to conceal itself from the decree; (4) נְסִיעָה — sudden travel to a distant place as the mechanism of that concealment; (5) הַנֶּפֶשׁ — the soul that subconsciously knows the decree and generates the travel-impulse; (6) פִּרְסוּם — the paradoxical increased publicity that can occur at the destination, which defeats the concealment; (7) הִסְתַּלְּקוּת (passing/death) of a tzaddik as the historical illustration. None of these are joined by bechina language. All are connected by narrative causality (eitza). Since there are no packages defined for this Torah, there are no additions to propose and no unassigned nodes.
